speakers.name: John Ternus
speakers.title: Incoming CEO (transitioning into role in September)

exchanges.question: No analyst question; IR handed to operator.

How much did demand outpace supply for iPhone and Mac in the March quarter, and is the June guide supply-constrained? Second: why drop the net cash neutral target, any change to capital return policy, and is investment organic or inorganic?
exchanges.answer: Cook: March constraints were primarily iPhone, lesser Mac, driven by availability of advanced nodes for SoCs; in June the majority of constraints will be on several Mac models, with less supply-chain flexibility than normal. Mac mini and Mac Studio demand (AI/agentic use) and MacBook Neo demand exceeded expectations; Mini and Studio may take several months to reach supply-demand balance; no quantification of unmet demand. Parekh: net cash neutral served well since 2018; evaluating cash and debt independently allows more optimal decisions while staying disciplined; remain committed to returning excess cash; over $1 trillion returned since program start, over $850 billion via buybacks; additional $100 billion authorization on top of leftover capacity. Organic vs inorganic not addressed.

exchanges.question: How should investors think about agents and an 'agentic smartphone'—new form factors? Second: gross margin philosophy after June given component costs; can Apple stay in a 47%-48% range or is there no visibility beyond June?
exchanges.answer: Cook declined to discuss the future road map, citing iPhone growth of 22% and the strongest cycle ever from launch through March quarter. On margins: minimal memory impact in December quarter; higher memory costs in March partially offset by carry-in inventory; June guide embeds significantly higher memory costs, partly offset by carry-in inventory. Beyond June, memory costs will drive an increasing impact on the business; Apple will evaluate and look at a range of options. No margin range given beyond June.

exchanges.question: How has MacBook Neo driven penetration in new segments (education, value, emerging markets) and how does the road map address underpenetrated markets? Second: was new App Store ad inventory a notable contributor to services growth, and what is the broader ad strategy with Maps ads coming this summer?
exchanges.answer: Cook: MacBook Neo is supply constrained; Apple undercalled enthusiasm; focus is customers new to Mac and long-time holders; schools like Kansas City Public Schools switching from Chromebooks and Windows, with growing anecdotes. Parekh: advertising grew year over year; added App Store search result ads; Apple Maps ads launch this summer in the U.S. and Canada; ads to respect privacy. Did not say whether App Store ads were a notable contributor; road map not discussed.

exchanges.question: With rising memory costs, will Apple prioritize share gain (holding prices, low end) or profitability? Second: which parts of the agentic AI stack will Apple build vs partner, where will it invest more, and is this tied to the net cash change (infrastructure build)?
exchanges.answer: Cook: will look at a range of options with memory costs increasing and would not go beyond that. Apple is clearly investing more, visible in OpEx; R&D is accelerating much faster than the company; investing in products and services. Parekh: AI investment is incremental on top of normal product road map investment. No link to net cash change or stack split given.

exchanges.question: What levers drive 20%+ iPhone growth despite supply constraints, and how durable is it? Second: what advice is Cook giving John Ternus for the transition?
exchanges.answer: iPhone 17 family drives growth: design, performance, durability, camera, Center Stage, integrated Apple Intelligence; double-digit growth in the majority of markets (U.S., Latin America, Greater China, Western Europe, India, Japan, Southeast Asia); March quarter record for upgraders; U.S. customer satisfaction 99%. Durability not addressed. Advice to Ternus: one of the most important decisions is where to spend his time, where the greatest benefit to the company and users is, and never forget the North Star of making the best products.

exchanges.question: Why is iPhone not constrained in June, and how is Apple securing SoCs and memory, including alternative memory sources? Second: is services gross margin nearing an asymptote, or is there further scaling leverage?
exchanges.answer: Cook: primary constraint in March and June quarters is advanced-node SoC availability, not memory; would not predict supply-demand matching; Mac mini and Mac Studio will take several months to balance; cause is undercalled demand plus lead times; majority of June constraint on Mac (Mac mini, Mac Studio, MacBook Neo). Alternative memory sources not addressed. Parekh: services portfolio has varied models and growth rates; Q2 services GM +20bp sequentially primarily mix; some services improving profitability with scale; hard to speculate on trajectory.

exchanges.question: How is Apple balancing the Google model collaboration with internal foundation models, and does it need to invest more? Follow-up: why was sequential product gross margin moderation muted this year (mix, FX), and what was the FX impact on gross margin?
exchanges.answer: Cook: investing more, R&D scaled significantly YoY; Google collaboration going well, happy with independent work. Parekh: products GM down 200bp sequentially on seasonal loss of leverage and higher memory costs; company GM +110bp sequentially from favorable mix and lower tariff-related costs, partly offset by seasonal deleverage and memory. Cook: 49.3% includes tariff costs, lower in March due to lower volume, full-quarter benefit of reduced IEEPA rates and reduced global rate under Section 122; applying for refunds via established processes and plans to reinvest any refunds into U.S. innovation and advanced manufacturing, additive to prior commitments. Parekh: no sequential FX impact on gross margin Q1 to Q2.

exchanges.question: What is Apple seeing in China, including competitive advantage from competitors' supply constraints? Second: how is the India opportunity evolving with a rising middle class?
exchanges.answer: Greater China grew 33% in the first half and 28% in the March quarter, a quarterly revenue record driven by iPhone (March quarter record); iPhone top-selling model in urban China, Mac mini top-selling desktop, MacBook Air top-selling laptop; store traffic up double digits. Competitor supply question not addressed. India is the second largest smartphone and third largest PC market; Apple still has modest share; majority of customers in all categories are new to the product; 'over the moon excited.'
